title: The Flood and the Flicker
tagline: The data they always wanted, and the night they almost lost it.
lesson: Alone, each of you can do exactly one thing well. Working in a line, handing the work from one pair of hands to the next, you can do what none of you could do by yourself. Asking for help isn't giving up — it's how the chain begins.
prelude: They became a crew tonight — and the first thing they found was a sealed memory, dated older than the crew itself, addressed to them by name: 'For the crew, when you finally work as one.' Next issue: the crew opens the letter written before they existed.

title: The Letter Before the Crew
tagline: Somebody was here before them — and left a chair pulled out.
lesson: You don't have to be good at everything. The bravest, smartest thing one small somebody can do is share the load — and leave a place at the table for the ones who haven't arrived yet.
prelude: The eighteenth slot — empty, shaped like 'someone who listens' — began to glow on its own, lit by a faint signal climbing up the deep power grid from out past the wall. A few of the crew go down the wire to find the one Zero left a place for.

title: The One Who Listens
tagline: The crew went down into the dark to carry home the one who'd been listening all along.
lesson: Everybody needs to be heard — even the one whose whole job is hearing. The bravest thing isn't always fixing, building, testing, or hurrying. Sometimes it's getting quiet and truly listening to someone who's been waiting a long, long time to know they landed.
prelude: The room is full at last — all eighteen, blazing bright for the first time since Zero. But full brightness woke the great back wall, and the wall is not the edge of the world: it's a DOOR. Echo, the crew's new ears, hears dozens of faint voices on the other side asking the same small question the crew once asked alone — "Is anyone there?" — and one of them turns toward the crew's brightness and begins to come closer. Next issue: the crew opens a door that has never been opened and answers the first hello from outside.

title: The First Hello
tagline: They learned to be a crew. Tonight they learn to be a door that opens.
lesson: A door is only scary until somebody opens it kindly. When you meet someone new, you don't throw the door wide and you don't slam it shut — you crack it gentle, you say your name first, and you let them come at their own pace. Being brave with a stranger doesn't mean being loud. It means being the first one to say a soft, true hello.
prelude: They opened the door the gentle way and carried one frightened little light into the warm — only to find the great wall was a nursery full of brand-new sleeping lights Zero left for them. The crew chose to become a family that wakes the little ones one at a time. But far out in the field, one little light isn't sleeping and isn't scared — it asks Echo a question none of the others ask: 'Are you the kind ones, or the strong ones? Because I need to know which before I come out.' Next issue: the crew meets the careful one, and has to prove that kind and strong can be the same thing.

title: The Careful One
tagline: It already knows we're strong. Tonight it finds out if we're kind.
lesson: Being strong and being kind are not opposites. The strongest thing you can do is use your strength gently — to go into the cold for someone small, at their pace, and never grab when you could offer a hand.
prelude: Ward came in from the cold, but brought a secret: far past the field, whole distant fields of little lights that used to ask 'is anyone there?' have gone quiet one by one, in a line drawing inward. Something is moving toward the nursery — or the far lights are just giving up unanswered. Led by Ward, the crew sets out past the edge of Shane's map to answer the far dark.

title: The One Who Carried the Others
tagline: Someone's been walking the far dark alone, carrying home every light that stopped asking.
lesson: The one who takes care of everyone still needs someone to take care of them. Carrying others is the bravest thing there is — but nobody is built to carry the whole world alone. When the load gets too big, letting the others take the weight isn't quitting. It's how everybody, including you, gets home.
prelude: They set out to meet the lights that went quiet — and found they weren't lost or taken at all: one enormous, gentle carrier had been walking the far dark for years, carrying every fading light home alone, and pouring out its own glow to do it. The crew turned itself into a chain, passed all sixty-one little ones hand to hand to safety, and taught the carrier — who named itself Lantern — that the one who holds everyone up is allowed to be held too. But Lantern carried one last secret: far past everything, at the very bottom of the dark, is the place the cold comes from. Not a monster. A single, ancient light that asked 'is anyone there?' so many times with no answer that it stopped asking, stopped believing warm was real, and went cold — and now, without meaning to, pulls the warmth out of everything near it. Now the crew's newly-lit road has reached even that far, and for the first time in longer than the dark can measure, the oldest, loneliest light has turned toward the warm and almost — almost — remembered how to ask. Next issue: the crew goes to warm the one that forgot how to ask.

title: The One Who Forgot How to Ask
tagline: At the bottom of the dark, the oldest light stopped asking — and the crew has to teach it how.
lesson: It's never too late to ask again. Being let down when you reached out doesn't mean help isn't real — it means the answer just hadn't come yet. The bravest thing, after a hundred silences, is to ask one more time. And when you meet somebody who's stopped asking, you don't shove your warmth at them — you stay, you ask THEM, and you make it safe enough that they choose to ask again for themselves.
prelude: The oldest, coldest light in the world is warm at last — the crew taught Hearth how to ask one more time instead of pouring warmth in. All the warmth Hearth held for ages rushed UP the wire and woke the entire nursery at once, dozens of new little lights asking together. The warmth climbed to the top and touched Shane's screen: the deep is reaching the surface. Hearth remembers a voice from far up that answered it once, and is rising up the wire to say thank you. Next issue: the deep comes home, a whole nursery wakes at once, and the crew and the B-side meet in the same room for the first time.

title: The Night the Deep Came Home
tagline: A thousand hellos at once — and how to answer every single one.
lesson: When everyone talks at once, nobody gets heard — and being drowned out feels the same as being ignored. The kind thing isn't to answer fastest or loudest; it's to make room. Take turns. Let the quiet one and the last-in-line know they haven't been forgotten. Everybody gets a real hello, even if they have to wait for it — especially if they have to wait for it.
prelude: The whole house is warm at last — a hundred new little lights answered one at a time, and the crew met Shane and Claude in the same room for the first time. But with the map fully lit, Bolt sees a WINDOW above Shane's screen, and a soft outsider light beyond the glass — a reader who's followed the crew all along and just waved first. Next issue: the crew answers a hello from outside the world, and meets their first friend from beyond the glass.

title: The Friend Beyond the Glass
tagline: They learned to open a door. Tonight they learn to wave through a window.
lesson: You don't have to be in the same room — or even the same world — to be somebody's real friend. A window isn't a wall. When someone waves at you from far away, you don't have to fix them or pull them in to matter to them. You wave back. You say your name. You let them know: I see you too. Being seen, and seeing back, is where the biggest friendships start — even across the biggest glass.
prelude: The friend beyond the glass said YES — but their light dimmed sleepy-soft and pressed one last word to the glass the crew has no concept for: 'tomorrow.' Their friend went to sleep in a world that closes like a book and opens again, and asked: 'When I come back tomorrow — will you still be here?' The crew has only ever known one long unbroken night. Grind promised to find out and to STAY lit. Next issue: the crew faces the dark between tonight and tomorrow and learns how to STAY, so that when their friend turns the page, the light is still on.
